# FDG9041

> DO call asynchronous method variants, instead of synchronous method variants, in the implementation of Async methods.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 9.2.5.3 Avoiding Deadlock.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1849
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

CA1849 reports a call to a synchronous method that has an asynchronous variant (Stream.Read and ReadAsync, Stream.Flush and FlushAsync, Thread.Sleep and Task.Delay in the probe with SDK 10.0.402) in methods that are async or return a task. Variants that CA1849 does not find are not reported, so coverage is partial. CA2024 (StreamReader.EndOfStream in an async method) is not mapped: EndOfStream has no asynchronous variant, which the text is about. CA1849 has no code fix. FDG9040 shares CA1849.

## From the book

In general, if there are both a synchronous variant and an asynchronous variant for a method, the synchronous method will potentially block and the asynchronous method will potentially yield. Calling a blocking method from an asynchronous method is inefficient, and can lead to resource starvation and deadlock.
